name: Wildfire smoke – long-range, national

geo.extent: All of Canada; most frequent in western and northern Canada, episodically in the east

description: Smoke from large fires travels thousands of kilometres. In 2023, Canada's record fire season (184,493 km² burned according to ECCC) cloaked much of the country in smoke; Montréal had the world's worst air quality on 25 June 2023. Cities far from forests can be affected.

exposed_areas: Prairie cities downwind of boreal fires
documented_events: 2023: smoke across Canada; Montréal worst air quality in the world on 25 June (ECCC 2023)
practical_implications: Plan indoor alternatives and air filtration for summer
Relevant for people with respiratory conditions; check the Air Quality Health Index

verification.notes: Event facts quoted or paraphrased from the cited official pages on 2026-10-30. Exposure and implications are agent-04 interpretation.

limitations: Smoke-day counts by station appear in the 1991–2020 clim records ("smoke or haze" days) where ECCC publishes them. Past events show exposure; they are not a prediction for any particular year. Exposure varies street by street – check municipal and provincial hazard maps for a specific property.
